report.summary: This frame is a clear Address setup with posture and limb angles largely within typical pro ranges. There are only mild deviations (a slightly greater spine tilt from vertical and a small right-knee difference versus the pro median); the shaft direction was estimated from the lead-arm pose. Overall the setup is serviceable but worth a quick check with the drills below.
coaching_recommendations: Check/maintain an athletic amount of knee flex: adopt the posture so you 'could jump' from it. Drill from p1_address_faults.md — assume your address with eyes closed, then open and confirm knees are bent enough that a gentle downward push wouldn’t tip you forward.

Confirm spine/head height and distance to the ball by letting the club set the spacing: place a club on the ground perpendicular to the target line and address so your hands rest roughly a hand’s-width above that club (this helps avoid over-bending or crowding the ball).

Verify shoulder tilt for a driver (or desired shot): hold a club along your shoulders and check in a mirror or video so the lead shoulder is slightly higher than the trail shoulder if you need an upward angle of attack — this is the recommended check in p1_address_faults.md.

report.summary: The frame is classified as Top (confidence 0.996). Measured joint angles (shoulders, spine, elbows, knees) all fall within typical pro ranges and the overall assessment is technically sound — no notable faults were detected. Shaft-direction estimates are unreliable for this frame so shaft comments are omitted.
coaching_recommendations: Reinforce a rotation-led backswing: continue to prioritize shoulder/torso rotation depth rather than trying to gain extra length with the arms — a useful practice is to make controlled backswings that stop when the lead arm reaches parallel (p4_top_faults.md).

Maintain the connection of the trail arm/elbow through the top — keep feeling the trail elbow 'pocketed' toward the trail hip; a simple drill is to swing with a headcover or glove tucked under the trail armpit to preserve that connection (p4_top_faults.md).

report.summary: This frame is Mid-downswing with high classifier confidence. Most joint angles fall inside typical pro ranges; there are only mild signs (hip_line and an estimated shaft direction) suggesting slightly limited hip clearance/rotation rather than a major fault. Recommendations focus on lower-body-first sequencing drills to ensure the hips lead the downswing.
coaching_recommendations: Initiate the downswing with the lead hip moving first — feel a small "bump" of the lead hip toward the target before the arms. Drill from the corpus: drop a pool ball behind the trail knee and start the downswing by moving the hips toward the target (over-the-top fix).
Practice "clearing the lead hip" using an alignment stick placed next to the lead hip; rotate the hip to touch the stick without sliding toward it (insufficient hip clearance fix).
If you suspect the hips are thrusting forward rather than rotating, use the wall/chair drill to feel rotation around a fixed axis rather than pushing toward the ball (early extension fix).

Note on the shaft: the club direction here is estimated from the lead-arm proxy (proxy_confidence=0.42), so treat any shaft-plane feedback as tentative. If you observe outside-to-in strikes on the course, prioritize the hip-bump and lead-hip clearing drills above to correct sequencing (over-the-top guidance).

report.summary: Frame classified as Address (high confidence). The setup is mostly within typical ranges except for a notable right-shoulder deviation that suggests the shoulder line or shoulder tilt at address is atypical; this can affect aim and initial swing plane. Focus on simple alignment and shoulder-tilt checks before addressing other mechanics.

key_deviations.explanation: The trail (right) shoulder angle is substantially lower than the pro typical range for Address, indicating the shoulder line may be misaligned (open/closed) or the shoulder tilt is atypical relative to the lead shoulder; this can produce aiming errors or compensations in the swing.

coaching_recommendations: Check alignment using a club laid on the ground parallel to the target line — the shoulder line should be parallel to that reference. Drill: practice setting up to a chair or wall and confirm the lead shoulder is not extended further forward than the trail shoulder relative to the wall (helps correct open/closed shoulder line).

For driver setup, ensure the lead shoulder is slightly higher than the trail shoulder (about 5–10° tilt away from the target) to pre-set an upward strike. Drill: hold a club along the shoulders and check the angle in a mirror or video to confirm shoulder tilt and symmetry.
